PASS, second RED, and this one is a REGRESSION TEST FOR A REAL DEFECT THE ACCEPTANCE TEST CANNOT SEE. Source-blind examiner Vera, spying only on the public Notification.requestPermission API from the page, found the tap handler re-invoked it on EVERY tap: four taps, four calls. It looked correct only because Chromium auto-suppresses a repeat prompt once permission is explicitly 'denied'. The harness drives a DISMISSAL ('default'), not a hard denial, and in that state a real device can genuinely show a second prompt. That is criterion 2 of this step ('the control does not ask for permission a second time'), the step's U8 observation ('por mas que toque no me vuelve a pedir el permiso') and decision 23's no-nagging rule, all three. Playwright's dialog listener never sees native permission prompts, so the acceptance oracle counts zero either way and would have shipped a nagging control on green. New unit test taps four times against a counting fake resolving 'default' and asserts exactly one call: RED exit 1, 'AssertionError: a control that keeps calling requestPermission after a dismissal is exactly the nagging decision 23 forbids', 4 !== 1. Deliberately uses 'default', never 'denied', because 'denied' is the state that masks the bug.

SECOND DEFECT, also found by the source-blind examiner and also invisible to the test suite by construction. After the no-re-ask fix the control was disabled in BEHAVIOUR but not in APPEARANCE: Vera measured computed styles on the built page and found background rgb(10,106,45) and colour rgb(255,255,255) UNCHANGED after the refusal, so the dead control still rendered in the same bold green as the live WhatsApp and Copiar buttons beside it. Her words: it still reads as an invitation to tap. ROOT CAUSE, a cascade specificity bug: the global convention in src/styles/components.css, button:disabled{background:var(--sunken);color:var(--ink-2)}, is specificity (0,1,1), while Astro's scoped .avisos-action[data-astro-cid-...]:disabled is (0,2,1), so the component's own border-only rule won and the global mute never applied. LANE PROCESS NOTE, worth keeping: the lane had already checked this and got it WRONG. Grepping the built CSS found the global rule present and concluded the button would mute. Presence in the stylesheet is not the same as winning the cascade; only a computed-style read on the real page settles it. Neither the unit layer nor the acceptance layer reads computed CSS, so nothing in the suite could have caught this.

PASS after the cascade fix, measured in a real browser on the built page because that is the only layer where this defect exists. Fix: the component's own scoped .avisos-action:disabled rule now sets background, colour AND border to the project's existing disabled tokens (--sunken / --ink-2); no new colours, no new copy, enabled state untouched. Built output confirms the emitted rule is .avisos-action[data-astro-cid-4xvpqd4c]:disabled{background:var(--sunken);color:var(--ink-2);border-color:var(--sunken)}. MEASURED before tap: background rgb(10,106,45), colour rgb(255,255,255), disabled false. AFTER tap, day: background rgb(227,239,243), colour rgb(59,90,99), disabled true, contrast 6.33:1. After tap, dark: background rgb(18,48,57), colour rgb(157,186,194), contrast 6.79:1. Both clear WCAG AA 4.5:1.
